title: CF Roadmap Sync prep — Jan 2026 (Asha personal notes)
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Time: Jan 13, 2026 09:30 - 10:30 PT
Attendees: product PMs (Maya), eng leads (Liam), applied-ml (Diego), infra (Priya), me (Asha) — plus optional: SRE (TBD)
Location: Zoom / notes into Confluence page (link above)

Purpose
- Align on top priorities for H1 2026 across product, serving runtime, and applied ML model onboarding.
- Resolve conflicts where product wants quick feature surface vs eng capacity and model quality work.
- Surface risks (latency regressions, cost increases) and agree on mitigations & owners.

Draft agenda (10 min each topical block)
1) Quick status snapshots (10m) — PM/Eng/ML highlight 1 blocker each (no slides):
   - PM: Hosted API priorities and customer commitments
   - Eng: major infra work (dedicated autoscaler, kernel tuning) affecting capacity
   - ML: model onboarding schedule + eval gaps (regression risk)
2) Prioritization discussion (25m) — propose ranked list and tradeoffs
   - Option A: Ship streaming + function-calling improvements end of Q1 (product asks)
   - Option B: Prioritize runtime kernel + batching improvements to reduce token cost by 15% (eng ask)
   - Option C: Invest in eval coverage + benchmark suite for new quantized model variants (applied-ml ask)
3) Capacity & rollout plan (10m) — dedicated lanes vs hosted fallback policies
4) Action items & owners (10m)
5) Parking lot / unresolved (5m)

Key prep notes (my mental checklist)
- Customers: top two customers expecting streaming+function-calling before end of Q1 (support tickets + sales notes). Confirm impact of delaying feature by 4–6 weeks.
- Engineering capacity: Liam indicated 3 engineers (2 infra, 1 runtime) available for feature work in Jan, then ramp to 6 in Feb after hiring.
- ML: Diego flagged that the new 3B quantized variant shows a 3–4% ROUGE drop on internal summarization evals (RDW-4123). We need regression guardrails before rollout.
- Costs: quantized variants reduce inference cost but increase infra testing overhead. Need a clear cost/quality tradeoff doc.

Open questions to surface in sync
- Which should be the gating metric for rollout of quantized model variants: token latency tail (p95) OR quality degradation vs baseline? (ask Applied ML)
- If we push runtime kernel work first, can product ship partial streaming improvements using existing code paths? (ask Eng)
- Timeline for Dedicated autoscaler changes — will that impact Hosted latency SLOs? (ask Infra/SRE)
- Does the ops team have bandwidth to run expanded eval harness for model variants in staging? (ask Solutions Eng / SRE)

Proposed decision framework (for triage during meeting)
- Rank by customer impact (hard commitments first) > risk to latency/cost (if high, deprioritize feature until mitigations exist) > cross-team unblocker cost (small wins that unblock many should be prioritized)
- If two items tie, prefer the one that reduces unit cost per token (helps economics).

Pre-read items I should mention quickly
- Confluence roadmap page summary (1-pager) — highlight the three proposed H1 pillars.
- RDW-4123 (ML regression) — brief summary: quantized 3B shows small QA drop on summarization, need more evals and maybe slight prompt tuning.
- RDW-4278 (Autoscaler design doc) — current proposal increases buffer for burst capacity; risk: higher idle cost, benefit: fewer timeouts.
- PR: serve#318 — kernel selection change prototype showing ~8% p95 improvements on A100 for long-context workloads.

My suggested starter proposal to present
- Short term (Q1): Ship streaming UX + function-calling MVP with gradual rollout behind feature flag, but gate full rollout on 1) p95 latency not increasing >10% and 2) no SMOKE regressions on key eval sets. Owned by Maya + Liam + Diego.
- Parallel: prioritize kernel/batching work for next two sprints with dedicated measurables (cost reduction target 12–15% on token cost for common workloads). Owned by Eng runtime team (Liam).
- ML: expand eval suite for quantized variants (add 3 new prompt sets, automated nightly runs in staging, regression alerting). Owned by Applied ML (Diego) with SRE support.

Quick notes-to-self for phrasing
- Emphasize: we can ship product-facing improvements behind flags but be explicit about the rollback plan + fallback model variants.
- Ask for concrete numbers not vague commitments ("how many engineers, how many sprints, measurable target").
- Push for a short-lived cross-team working group (2-week cadence) to validate quality and performance tradeoffs before large rollouts.

Proposed action items to assign in meeting
- Maya: finalize customer commitments doc and share updated priority matrix by Jan 15. (link to customer notes)
- Liam: share sprint plan for kernel/batching work and list of required infra changes by Jan 16. Attach RDW-4278.
- Diego: commit to expanding eval harness and smoke tests; deliver test plan + quick proof-of-concept runs by Jan 20. Reference RDW-4123.
- Priya: confirm SRE support window for expanded nightly evals and estimate cost impact (hours & infra) by Jan 18.
- Me (Asha): run the cross-team WG kickoff if approved, create Confluence meeting notes and track action items.

Risk log (short)
- Risk: shipping streaming changes without kernel optimizations could cause p95 regressions for long-tail customers. Mitigation: feature flags + canary on small customer cohort.
- Risk: quantized models cause quality regressions not caught by current evals. Mitigation: enlarge eval sets + add human review sample.
- Risk: increased infra cost from autoscaler buffer. Mitigation: simulate cost with current traffic and include rollback threshold.

Parking lot (to raise if time)
- Should we prioritize dedicated capability for top enterprise customer vs platform-wide optimizations? (possible sales ask)
- Longer-term: invest in deploy-time model verification (binary that runs quick validation on new model images) — note to add to backlog.

Notes to self: keep meeting tight, call for decisions not just updates. If we can't decide, define experiment and owners.

End of notes.
summary: Personal prep notes for CF roadmap sync: agenda, open questions, suggested decisions, action items and owners; focuses on tradeoffs between shipping product features (streaming/function-calling), runtime kernel/batching improvements, and expanded evals for quantized model variants.
